text: 🇲🇽✊ "The pride of being Mexican is enormous. It wasn't like that in the neoliberal era." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 Asked about the contrast between the public response to Calderón and to López Obrador, who presented a new book on Sept 30, Sheinbaum first condemned any violence, including what was done to a Calderón statue at Los Pinos. She said the PRIAN is no longer widely accepted "because people's lives have changed, and so has their consciousness," and recalled the phrase "only the people can save the people." "Today we say it to the four winds: I am Mexican. That strength is invincible."

🇲🇽✊ "They took the Yaquis to Quintana Roo, to Yucatán, to be slaves during the Porfiriato on the henequen haciendas." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 Asked about her Sept 26 visit to Sonora, Sheinbaum recalled John Kenneth Turner's "Barbarous Mexico." Turner posed as a US hacienda owner in Yucatán and documented slavery that had been formally abolished since Vicente Guerrero. Many of the enslaved were Yaqui and Maya. Under the Yaqui Justice Plan, lands have been returned, water is reaching most communities, there is a university, and schools are being improved.

text: 🇲🇽💜 "There wasn't a single woman in the civic calendar, only men, as if there were only heroes and no heroines of the nation." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 On the second anniversary of taking office, Sheinbaum was asked what has changed for women. Today 24 women are in the civic calendar, and the mañanera's "Women in History" segment has presented 93 stories. She also cited the pension for women aged 60 to 64, equality written into the Constitution, and the new law on femicide. For girls and boys, she said, simply seeing a woman president "changes their mentality."

🇲🇽🏭 "Money was even given to transnationals by CONACYT with the idea of promoting innovation. In reality, they never promoted any innovation that we know of." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 1, 2026 Under the new model, Olinia, the Mexican electric mini-vehicle, is a public development by public researchers: some 70 university research groups working on electromobility joined forces in Puebla to build it. Once the public design and patents exist, private companies are invited into a mixed venture for production. "It's not giving the resource to private enterprise so it can develop innovation."

text: 🇲🇽🔬 "It sometimes sounds very difficult for us to become a scientific and technological power, but we have everything to do it." — Rosaura Ruiz, Secretary of Science, Humanities, Technology and Innovation In 2026, research projects received 1,676 million pesos more than in 2025. Approved projects rose 48%, there are more than 100,000 graduate scholarships, and public research centers received 200 new positions, their first real expansion since most were founded in the 1970s. Strategic projects include Olinia (Mexican electric mini-vehicle), Kutsari (semiconductors), Coatlicue (Latin America's most powerful supercomputer) and an Earth-observation satellite constellation.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Remittances Dip in August, Still Up 2.2% for the Year</u>

Mexico received $5.452 billion in remittances in August, down 3.6% year on year, which ends a six-month growth streak, El Financiero reports from Banxico data. The number of transfers fell 6.4% to 13.24 million, but the average transfer rose 3% to $412.

January through August, migrant families sent home $41.8 billion, up 2.2%. Under ICE raids and Trump's remittance tax, Mexicans abroad are sending less often but sending more each time.

🇲🇽🔬 <u>Mexico's Science Fund Jumps 111%</u>

Secihti chief Rosaura Ruiz reported during the review of Sheinbaum's Second Report that research, development and innovation projects have an extra 1.676 billion pesos in 2026, a 111% increase over 2025. That money funds 1,340 new technology and innovation projects, and 44.7% of their lead investigators are women.

The fund also supports 3,142 ongoing research projects, more than 100,000 graduate scholarships and 13 national strategic projects. The neoliberal decades starved Conacyt. This government is funding science.
